scope.note: This worksheet describes the full source manifest. Store distributions may remove a site; reconcile each generated manifest and listing before submission.

permissions.name: nativeMessaging
permissions.purpose: Send selected download tasks, applicable cookies, and optional media metadata to the locally installed com.clipgo.host helper; receive progress, titles, errors, paths, and helper status; request folder selection, file reveal, and engine updates.

permissions.name: storage
permissions.purpose: Persist tasks and preferences in chrome.storage.local. No chrome.storage.sync use is implemented.

permissions.name: contextMenus
permissions.purpose: Offer download actions for supported video links and the current supported page.

permissions.name: cookies
permissions.purpose: Read target-site cookies for user-requested downloads with the existing browser login. Cookie values can be authentication credentials; they are passed to the local helper and used with target website requests.

permissions.name: notifications
permissions.purpose: Display completion messages, which may include video titles, and context-menu operation errors. Completion notifications respect the notify preference.

permissions.name: activeTab
permissions.purpose: Read the current tab's URL/title when the user opens the popup to identify an eligible video.

dataHandling.access: Supported page DOM links, video identifiers, readable titles, player elements, user-pasted links, and context-menu targets. Links may contain site access tokens; Xiaohongshu xsec_token is retained.
dataHandling.purpose: Identify the selected video, offer a download action, name files, show progress, and retry the same item.
dataHandling.storage: Selected URLs and titles are stored in extension task history. Current page detection also uses transient memory.
recipients: target website and its APIs/CDNs during the download
evidence: extension/content.js: currentVideoInfo and DOM title detection

dataHandling.access: Normal same-origin video API JSON responses and RENDER_DATA; exact video ID, title, HTTPS douyinvod.com media URL and up to 16 formats. Responses are bounded to 2 MiB; up to 100 parsed records are held in page memory.
dataHandling.purpose: Use the exact selected video's normal webpage media source when available; resolve the exact requested direct watch page for retries.
dataHandling.storage: Transient page and background memory, then a temporary helper info JSON file. Direct media URLs are not intentionally persisted as extension task fields; error output can still contain URLs.
dataHandling.ordinaryCurrentVideoGuard: Media is bound to a matching, visible, loaded video owner. A dedicated exact /video/id page lookup can use matching initial/observed metadata without visible playback.

dataHandling.collectionTrigger: A user-requested download using the standard extractor path. An available Douyin page-media source skips this export.

siteRules.youtube: youtube.com only when ytCookies is true; default false

dataHandling.localTransfer: Browser Native Messaging to the installed helper, then a Netscape-format temporary cookie file for yt-dlp.
dataHandling.networkUse: The engine sends applicable cookies to target sites according to cookie scope and site authentication flow. Cookies can therefore leave the device. They are not sent to a ClipGo-operated service.
dataHandling.tencentSpecialHandling: Relevant v.qq.com cookie login fields are mapped to logintoken and sent to Tencent's first-party video API. The plugin does not broaden cookie-jar domains or copy Cookie headers to a CDN. API errors in that login-token path are replaced with a generic message to avoid exposing that query.
dataHandling.storage: Not intentionally persisted in extension task records or settings. Temporary cookie file removal is attempted in finally; abrupt process termination or deletion failure can leave it behind.

dataHandling.retention: Trim to at most 30 finished tasks when a new task starts, preserving active tasks. Completion can temporarily leave more than 30 finished entries. User can remove one finished task or clear all finished tasks. Preferences remain until reset or browser extension data removal.
dataHandling.network: No task-history synchronization or upload is implemented. A selected task URL is used again when retrying.
evidence: extension/background.js: MAX_TASKS, persist, startDownload, remove, clearFinished

dataHandling.location: Chosen download directory, default ~/Downloads/ClipGo; helper config.json stores downloadDir.
dataHandling.retention: Files remain until the user deletes them. Failed/cancelled downloads can leave partial media files. Removing task history does not delete files. Windows helper uninstall preserves config.json, host.log, downloaded media and unknown user files.
dataHandling.network: Media is downloaded from the target site/CDN, not uploaded by ClipGo.

dataHandling.location: host.log in the helper directory; clipgo_*.txt and clipgo_media_*.json in the system temporary directory; local installation logs and engine update staging files.
dataHandling.contents: Host version, timestamps, task ID, task URL, quality, exception details and the last 30 download-engine output lines on failure. Errors may contain titles, local paths, resource URLs or signed parameters. Installer logs can contain local paths and installation errors.
dataHandling.retention: host.log is deleted before the next write after its existing size exceeds 1,000,000 bytes, with no time expiry. Cookie/info temporary files are deleted on normal task cleanup; crashes or deletion failures may leave them. macOS engine update staging is removed in finally. Download engine cache and partial files have separate lifetimes.
dataHandling.sharing: No automatic log or crash upload is implemented. Users should review and redact logs before manually sharing them.

dataHandling.access: yt-dlp may retain downloaded information such as client IDs and signatures in its default local cache.
dataHandling.retention: ClipGo's command does not disable the engine cache. It is outside extension task cleanup and Windows helper inventory uninstall.

serverAndAnalytics.note: These are implementation observations, not a claim that no personal data is accessed, processed, locally stored, or sent to target websites.

userRequestedEngineUpdate.windows: Execute bundled yt-dlp -U; upstream updater contacts its official release infrastructure and replaces the native executable.
userRequestedEngineUpdate.macOS: Download the latest official yt-dlp_macos.zip from GitHub into a temporary directory, verify the executable runs with --version, then replace the local engine.
userRequestedEngineUpdate.note: An engine update can change native extraction/network behavior independently of the extension version.

remoteExecutableCode.extension: No remote executable-code loading is implemented; scripts are packaged in the extension.
remoteExecutableCode.nativeHelper: The helper runs installed native tools and can replace yt-dlp after a user-requested update. This must be disclosed separately from extension scripts.
remoteExecutableCode.ejs: Official yt-dlp executables bundle EJS, which works with a local JavaScript runtime to process site-provided player/challenge scripts. Current ClipGo download commands use local Deno where present, do not enable --remote-components, and include --ignore-config. Upstream also supports optional ejs:github and ejs:npm remote fetching, which is not enabled by this command.
